title: Approximation reduction of regular alteration coverings to complete normal local bases
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$. For a reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme $S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible and a nowhere dense closed subset $Z$, write $U_\ell(S,Z)$ for the following proposition: there is a finite covering family $(T_i\to S)_i$ in $\operatorname{alt}/S$ for the topology of $\ell'$-alterations, with every $T_i$ regular Noetherian and the inverse image of $Z$ the support of a strict normal crossings boundary. Empty boundaries are allowed. If $U_\ell(S,Z)$ holds for all normal complete local Noetherian schemes $S$ and all such $Z$, it holds for every reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian $S$ and every such $Z$. There is also a bounded version: for any integer $d\geq0$, it is enough to know this proposition for normal complete local $S$ of Krull dimension at most $d$ to obtain it for all reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian $S$ of dimension at most $d$. No global finite dimension assumption is required in the unbounded assertion. Complete local means that the affine local ring is complete for powers of its maximal ideal; normal means its local rings are integrally closed domains. Krull dimension is the supremum of lengths of chains of irreducible closed subsets.

Conventions for the notions used here: [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Expose III Proposition 6.2 and its proof, printed pp. 43--45, including the reduction to normal complete local schemes on p. 44; bounded form as applied in IX 1.3, p. 132. The bounded argument uses completions of local rings, which have the same dimension, and normalization, which is finite in this setting.

proof.text: First prove the assertion for $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ normal excellent henselian Noetherian local and $Z$ nowhere dense. By [lem-per-henselian-normal-completion-preparation], $\widehat A$ is a normal Noetherian local domain and $\widehat Z$ is nowhere dense. By [lem-per-complete-local-excellence], $\widehat A$ is excellent, so the assumed complete-normal-local assertion applies and supplies a finite alteration covering $(\widehat X_i\to\widehat S)_i$ by regular schemes with boundaries $\widehat D_i$ of supports $\widehat Z\times_{\widehat S}\widehat X_i$.

source.place: III Proposition 6.2, p.44, passage from normal henselian excellent A to its completion

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-marked-finite-diagram-approximation] to this finite family and all the components and intersections of the $\widehat D_i$. It gives one finite type $A$-algebra model and a threshold for which every sufficiently close section has regular open neighborhoods of the entire closed fibres, with the marked strict normal crossings boundaries supported on the inverse image of $Z$. Apply [lem-per-alteration-cover-approximation] to that model, increasing the index and the congruence threshold if necessary. It gives a second threshold ensuring that the reduced dominant parts of its pulled-back members form an alteration covering. Choose a common index and the maximum of the two thresholds; both conclusions then hold for the same section.

Write this finite type model algebra as $A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$; the ideal of relations is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], since $A$ is Noetherian. Its structural map to $\widehat A$ gives a solution of all the $f_j$. Excellence includes the G-ring condition by [def-exc-excellent-ring], and $A$ is henselian. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-approximation], applied to the pair $(A,\mathfrak m)$ and the threshold $N$ from Step 2, gives a solution in $A$ congruent to the completed solution modulo $\mathfrak m^N\widehat A$. Evaluation factors through the displayed quotient because all relations vanish; this is the required $A$-algebra section $u$. This preserves the single common model and hence every marked inclusion and intersection simultaneously.

source.place: III section 2, p.36, Artin approximation of the section; Stacks Tag 0AH5, lemma-henselian-pair, case (2)

proof.text: Proceed by strong induction on $d=\dim S$ for the bounded assertion. The case $d=0$ is immediate. For $d>0$, after Steps 1--3 we have the finite alteration family $(P_i\to S)_i$ and regular marked open neighborhoods $V_i$ of their closed fibres. For every non-closed point $t\in S$, the local ring $\mathcal O_{S,t}$ has dimension $<d$; the induction hypothesis applied to its henselian and complete-normal-local reductions gives a finite regular marked alteration covering of the corresponding henselian local scheme. The prescribed-family spreading theorem [lem-per-henselian-regular-pair-spreading] spreads this covering, including all boundary components and intersections, to a pointed separated etale neighborhood $T_t\to S$ with residue field unchanged. Their restrictions $T_t\times_S(S\setminus\{s\})$ form an etale family over the Noetherian open subscheme $S\setminus\{s\}$ that is completely decomposed pointwise (each non-closed $t$ has the point $t'$ with unchanged residue field); [lem-per-completely-decomposed-etale-finite-subcover] on $S\setminus\{s\}$ extracts finitely many of them. The closed point need not lie under these $T_t$; it is handled by the $V_i$. Apply [lem-per-alteration-cover-closed-fibre-shrink] to the closed-fibre neighborhoods $V_i$ and these finitely many pointwise families. Its conclusion says that the dominant components of the $V_i$ together with the composites of the spread covers form a finite alteration covering of $S$, with regular sources and the required strict normal crossings boundaries. This is the dimension-inductive replacement for the invalid assertion that arbitrary open neighborhoods of closed fibres preserve an $\ell'$-alteration covering.

source.place: III Proposition 6.2, p.44; corrected dimension-induction argument required after the prime-to-ell shrinking counterexample

proof.text: Now let $T$ be any reduced quasi-excellent Noetherian scheme and fix $t\in T$. Apply [lem-per-henselian-normal-completion-preparation] to $R=\mathcal O_{T,t}$. It gives a reduced excellent ordinary henselization $H$ and its finite componentwise normalization $\coprod_a\operatorname{Spec}B_a\to\operatorname{Spec}H$, with every $B_a$ normal excellent henselian local. The inverse images of $Z$ remain nowhere dense. Step 4 supplies regular-pair alteration coverings of all these finitely many $\operatorname{Spec}B_a$. By [lem-per-alteration-cover-calculus], the reduced component family covers $\operatorname{Spec}H$, and each normalization map over its component is a proper birational singleton covering (it is finite birational by the preparation lemma). Compose these coverings and the regular-pair coverings. Their sources and boundaries are the same schemes and boundaries, so this gives $U_\ell(\operatorname{Spec}H,Z_H)$.

source.place: III Proposition 6.2, pp.43--44, henselian and normalization reductions

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-henselian-regular-pair-spreading] to the finite family just obtained. It supplies a pointed etale neighborhood $(T'_t,t')\to(T,t)$ with unchanged residue field and a finite regular-pair alteration covering over $T'_t$, with boundary exactly over the inverse image of $Z$. As $t$ varies, these pointed neighborhoods form a completely decomposed etale family: the chosen point over each $t$ has the same residue field. By [lem-per-completely-decomposed-etale-finite-subcover], finitely many of these neighborhoods still form a completely decomposed family. Such a family covers for the alteration topology by [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. Compose its finite regular-pair coverings using [lem-per-alteration-cover-calculus]. All composites are finite type, generically finite and maximally dominant since this holds for alteration objects and for etale maps on a reduced base. The resulting finite family proves $U_\ell(T,Z)$.

source.place: III Proposition 6.2, first paragraph, pp.43--44; II 2.2.4 and the topology generators

proof.text: For the bounded form, assume the complete-normal-local assertion only in dimensions at most $d$. If $\dim T\leq d$, each local ring $R=\mathcal O_{T,t}$ has dimension at most $d$: a chain of primes in $R$ gives a chain of specializations in $T$. The preparation lemma [lem-per-henselian-normal-completion-preparation] gives $\dim B_a\leq\dim H=\dim R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension], $\dim\widehat B_a=\dim B_a\leq d$. Hence every use of the hypothesis in Step 1 is legitimate; Steps 2--6 use no uniformization hypothesis on any larger-dimensional base. They descend finite data and do not apply the hypothesis to the intermediate finite type model schemes. In the unbounded case no common bound on $\dim\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is needed. If $T$ is empty use the empty covering; $Z=\varnothing$ uses the empty marking throughout, and $d=0$ causes no exception.

source.place: III Proposition 6.2 and its use in IX 1.3, p.132; boundedness follows on the actual local completions used

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q142-e537bd1c3 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Re-delivery after the f16446a6 RETURN, which found the old closed-fibre shrink lemma false. Four new nodes are unchanged from that delivery and the item statement is unchanged; I reread all four against ILO III 3.1, 5.1, 5.4 and 6.2 (pp.43-45), III 6.3 and EGA IV 18.7.6. The replaced node lem-per-alteration-cover-closed-fibre-shrink is now a dimension-inductive gluing lemma, and it is true apart from one clause. Why it is true: on each P_i, the family made of V_i and the base changes P_i x_S T_t is completely decomposed etale, because points over s lie in V_i and points over t != s lift with unchanged residue field. So it covers by def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology (i); composing with the Q_tj and refining gives a cover of S. The two earlier counterexamples do not meet the new hypotheses. The false clause: the node said a finite subfamily of the T_t is completely decomposed over S, but the T_t exist only for non-closed t, so nothing need lie over s (DVR with T_eta = Spec K). Fixed: the node now says the subfamily is completely decomposed over the punctured scheme S minus s, with the finite set F found by II 2.2.4 there. Item Step 4 had the same wording; it now extracts on S minus s and leaves the closed point to the V_i. I also corrected the node's source place: ILO p.44 has no dimension induction, because it invokes II 4.1.1, which is proved only for alt. The repair is built from ILO's own Nisnevich spreading in the first paragraph of 6.2. Steps 1-3 and 5-7 check out: Artin approximation for (A,m) uses excellence to get a G-ring, the induction for the bounded form is valid, and the unbounded case is local. I accepted the three generic pbc algebra tool_uses. Batch-5 flags: the henselization definition and the SNC-boundary definition are general definitions. Stacks 01TE (a finite-residue point is closed in its fibre, reached through alteration-cover-calculus) and 00NM (regular rings are universally catenary, reached through complete-local-excellence) are pure algebra and not part of the trace-formula or Poincare-duality proofs; all accepted. No duplicates found among the alteration, standard-form and cd-etale nodes. Fixes: two whole JSON files under fixes/dag/nodes/sec-deligne-laumon-a1/.; 2 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
